title: Making Operational States Explicit: A Unified Framework for State-Aware Object-Centric Process Mining
content: Object-centric process mining preserves shared events and relationships among objects whose lifecycles overlap. The conditions of these objects may remain implicit in their activities, measurements, and relationships. We present State-Aware Object-Centric Process Mining (SA-OCPM), a framework for defining operational states and tracking them over time. States can be specified through domain rules or learned from event histories. The framework associates states with individual objects at shared events and can combine the states of related objects. It measures how long conditions persist and characterizes behavior within and between states. FLOWVAULT implements the main analyses in a browser workbench for Object-Centric Event Log (OCEL) 2.0 data. We use synthetic inventory management and manufacturing logs with independently computed references. The tested rule-based state assignments and transitions agree exactly with these references. The analyses quantify time in undesirable conditions and time to recovery. Learned states show limited agreement with simulated operating regimes. Prediction on future data remains unverified, and broad violation rules produce many false alarms. Tested command-line operations finish within seconds on logs with up to 300,000 events. The results support descriptive analysis of operational states. Decision support requires further validation with organizational data.
